description: The forecast for a stretch of time: "What's Saturday looking like?", "What will conditions be between 6 PM and midnight?", "this weekend". Give start_time (and optionally end_time or duration_hours). Returns a one-line summary, the temperature range, rain, wind, any conditions worth acting on, and the hourly and daily rows. The forecast reaches about seven days. Beyond that it says so and does not guess.

duration_hours.description: Instead of end_time: how many hours to cover.

end_time.description: When the period ends, in the same formats as start_time. "midnight" means the next midnight.

latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Use with longitude instead of location.

location.description: A place name such as "Glenbeulah, WI" or "Greenbush, Wisconsin", or coordinates as "43.79,-88.05". Add the state or country for small towns, because a bare "Greenbush" matches several places.

longitude.description: Longitude in degrees, west negative. Use with latitude instead of location.

start_time.description: When the period starts. Defaults to now. An ISO 8601 time such as 2026-10-03T18:00:00-05:00 (read in the place's own time zone when it has no offset), or plain words: "now", "tonight", "tomorrow morning", "Saturday", "6 PM", "between 6 PM and midnight". A bare hour with no AM or PM is refused rather than guessed.

units.description: imperial (F, mph, inches) or metric (C, km/h, mm). Defaults to imperial in the United States and metric elsewhere.

name: get_forecast
title: Forecast for a time period
